newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Minister reassures unions on S.Africa budget.
newsitem.headline: Minister reassures unions on S.Africa budget.

text.p: Labour Minister Tito Mboweni sought to reassure leftist unions on Wednesday that South Africa's 1997/98 budget would address their concerns, but he acknowledged there were differences of approach.

"There will of course be differences in terms of our approach here and there, on tax, a difference here and there between our approaches to exchange controls, but the fundamental approach is what all of us here would want to see," Mboweni said.

He was speaking after accepting a memorandum from public sector unions within the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) which organised a demonstration of about 1,500 people outside parliament to coincide with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's presentation of the budget.
The memorandum demanded higher corporate taxes, a special tax on the "super rich", a capital gains tax and a luxury goods tax.
It described the current 45 percent tax on high income earners as too low. Anyone making more than 200,000 rand a year should be taxed 55 percent, the memorandum said.
"Most of the elements contained in the memorandum have been accommodated," Mboweni said.

"There'll be significant movement towards ensuring the needs of our people will be met... Let none of us believe all the problems of our country can be solved by the minister of finance this afternoon," he said.

"We must be careful when we look at numbers, when somebody says 'you should just increase expenditure', and you don't look at the capacity of the government to actually spend the money, what you are saying is 'go and borrow the money, and pay the interest', and yet that money is not used," Mboweni said.
This would increase South Africa's debt burden, he added.
